title: MariaDB Small Examples
description: Use these small MariaDB examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Check your database session
examples.description: A database client sends SQL to the MariaDB server.
examples.code: SELECT VERSION() AS server_version,DATABASE() AS current_database;
examples.output: The result identifies your MariaDB version and selected database. The database value is NULL if none is selected.

examples.title: Create an InnoDB sample table
examples.description: InnoDB is a storage engine that supports transactions and foreign keys.
examples.code: CREATE TABLE cma_maria_books(id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,title VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,pages INT) ENGINE=InnoDB;
examples.output: The practice database now has an empty book table with an automatic id column.

examples.title: Insert a row and read its id
examples.description: After an insert in the same connection, LAST_INSERT_ID can report the automatically generated id.
examples.code:
INSERT INTO cma_maria_books(title,pages) VALUES('Moon Trip',60);
SELECT LAST_INSERT_ID() AS new_book_id;
examples.output: The result is the id generated for that insert in this session.

examples.title: Search a lowercase form
examples.description: LOWER makes text lowercase for a comparison.
examples.code: SELECT title FROM cma_maria_books WHERE LOWER(title) LIKE 'moon%';
examples.output: The sample Moon Trip row matches the lowercase moon pattern.

examples.title: Take a sorted sample
examples.description: ORDER BY arranges rows before LIMIT chooses a few.
examples.code: SELECT title,pages FROM cma_maria_books ORDER BY pages,title LIMIT 3;
examples.output: The query returns at most three rows with the smallest page counts first.

examples.title: Join grouped text
examples.description: GROUP_CONCAT joins text values from a group into one string.
examples.code:
WITH books AS (SELECT 'story' AS kind,'Moon Trip' AS title UNION ALL SELECT 'story','Tiny Seed')
SELECT kind,GROUP_CONCAT(title ORDER BY title SEPARATOR ', ') AS titles FROM books GROUP BY kind;
examples.output: The story group has the text Moon Trip, Tiny Seed.

examples.title: Use a short recursive query
examples.description: A recursive CTE can use earlier results to make later ones.
examples.code: WITH RECURSIVE numbers(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 FROM numbers WHERE n<4) SELECT n FROM numbers;

examples.title: Check JSON text
examples.description: MariaDB can work with JSON text using JSON functions.
examples.code: SELECT JSON_VALID('{"title":"Moon Trip"}') AS valid_json,JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT('{"title":"Moon Trip"}','$.title')) AS title;
examples.output: valid_json is 1 and title is Moon Trip.

examples.title: Handle a duplicate key deliberately
examples.description: ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE changes a row when an insert meets an existing unique key.
examples.output: Mia's points become 5 rather than creating a second row with the same key.

examples.title: Undo row changes in a transaction
examples.description: A transaction on InnoDB can undo row changes before they are committed.
examples.output: The final count is 0 after the insert is rolled back.

examples.title: Inspect the actual table rules
examples.description: SHOW CREATE TABLE prints the database's stored definition.
examples.output: The result includes the practice table definition as MariaDB stores it.

examples.title: Make a practice database backup
examples.description: A logical dump writes SQL that can recreate database objects and rows.
examples.output: The client asks for a password and writes a dump of the named practice database to a local file.
